problem_statement:
An application using NuttX work queue interfaces observes incomplete and inconsistent behavior for handle-based custom work queues. In a flat or kernel build with CONFIG_SCHED_WORKQUEUE, an application can create a custom queue with work_queue_create() and then submit work with work_queue_wq() or work_queue_next_wq(). If the delay argument is invalid, especially a negative delay or a delay beyond the supported watchdog limit WDOG_MAX_DELAY, the call is not consistently rejected with -EINVAL. The caller can observe a non-error result, so applications relying on argument validation fail.

The kernel must expose the full public contract for dynamically created custom work queues in both flat/kernel and protected/user configurations. work_queue_create() must create a custom queue with the requested name, priority, stack address, stack size, and worker count. Invalid arguments, such as a NULL name, non-positive stack size, invalid worker count, or unsupported configuration, must cause creation to fail and return NULL. work_queue_priority_wq() must return the worker priority for a valid custom queue handle and must return -EINVAL for a NULL or otherwise invalid handle.

For queue-ID interfaces, work_queue() and work_queue_next() must continue to support the predefined HPWORK, LPWORK, and USRWORK queues and must reject invalid queue IDs, NULL work structures, NULL worker callbacks, negative delays, and delays beyond WDOG_MAX_DELAY with -EINVAL. The same validation must apply to handle-based work_queue_wq() and work_queue_next_wq() for custom queues. Cancelling work that is not currently queued must be a successful no-op returning OK, while invalid handle, queue ID, or work structure arguments must return -EINVAL. work_cancel_sync() and work_cancel_sync_wq() must cancel pending work and wait for callbacks already using that same work structure to finish, and must not deadlock when called from the callback using that work structure.

In protected or kernel builds with CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK, the user-mode work queue support must not be limited only to the predefined USRWORK queue. Custom user work queues must be available through work_queue_create(), work_queue_free(), work_queue_wq(), work_queue_next_wq(), work_cancel_wq(), work_cancel_sync_wq(), and work_queue_priority_wq(). Custom user queues require pthread support and must create a configurable worker pool. The predefined USRWORK queue must still work with the queue-ID APIs.

Destruction must only succeed for dynamically created custom queues. work_queue_free() must return -EINVAL for a NULL handle or for predefined HPWORK, LPWORK, or USRWORK queues, and must return -EDEADLK when called from one of the queue's own worker callbacks. It must discard pending work, make the associated work structures available for reuse before returning, wait for running callbacks and all worker threads to finish, and invalidate the handle. After teardown has begun, work_queue_wq() and work_queue_next_wq() must reject new submissions with -ESHUTDOWN. Pending replacement must replace an already pending instance of the same work structure on the same queue rather than duplicating or losing it, and work_queue_next_wq() must schedule relative to the previous expiration time so periodic requeue does not accumulate callback execution time. User-mode custom queue APIs must be task-context only and must not be called from an interrupt handler, while flat/kernel queue and cancel submission paths may remain interrupt-safe where already specified. Existing HPWORK, LPWORK, and USRWORK facilities must continue to work.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The ostest wqueue test must exercise dynamically created work queues (one and two workers) and the hardened queue lifecycle: invalid-argument validation, explicit caller priority lookup, immediate/delayed work, pending replacement and cancellation, callback-driven periodic requeue, synchronous and parallel cancellation of concurrent callbacks using one work_s, multiple simultaneous custom queues, callback self-destruction rejection (-EDEADLK), and queue teardown that rejects requeue (-ESHUTDOWN) and waits for running callbacks. On the pre-fix kernel the scheduler custom-queue lifecycle and cancellation behavior do not match these expectations, so the test's assertions fail; the test must pass once the kernel provides the hardened custom-queue behavior.
